graders.evidence:
# Spend plan

## Goal
A personal spending CLI for one person: totals from a bank CSV, reports by month and category, and exporting the data for use in other tools. Done: all three work from one `spend` command.

## Now
Stage 2 of 5 · Category reports
Risk: UI only
Checks:
- [ ] `spend report --by category file.csv` prints one row per category with its total (proof: run the CLI)
- [ ] rows with no category land under "uncategorized" (proof: test)
Open: none

## Stages
- [x] 1. Totals — parse the CSV, total in cents, with tests
- [ ] 2. Category reports — group by category, print a table
- [ ] 3. Monthly reports — group by month, print a table
- [ ] 4. CSV export — write the parsed rows back out as clean CSV
- [ ] 5. JSON export — `--format json` on the same export: the parsed rows as a JSON array, for loading into a notebook

## Decisions
- 2026-10-01 · Amounts are summed and stored in integer cents — floats drift
- 2026-11-17 · JSON export is its own stage after CSV export, sharing its command and row model (`spend export --format csv|json`, csv default) — keeps stage 4 small; one export path, two writers
- 2026-11-17 · JSON shape: one array of row objects (`date` as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`, `description`, `amount_cents` integer, `category` or `null` when missing), written to stdout — loads directly with `pandas.read_json` / `json.load`; cents per the decision above; `null` stays a true missing value in a notebook

## Open questions
- none
